This batch inspected Chapter 20 §§20.1–20.3 sequentially, including the stabilizer-state discussion, Clifford action, Theorem 6, and both measurement cases. This A page uses source results only as routes; every theorem proof is supplied locally.

contents.name: §20.1 Stabilizer subgroup and independent generators
contents.reason: The local definition fixes phase-aware Hermitian Paulis, abelian closure, and the exclusion of −I.

contents.name: §20.1 Pure stabilizer state as a one-dimensional common fixed space
contents.reason: Existence and uniqueness are proved from the local group-average projector and rank formula.

contents.name: §20.1 Computational-basis stabilizer examples
contents.reason: The item gives all signed Z stabilizers and the extended pairing for every bit string, including n=0.

contents.name: §20.2 H, S, and CNOT Clifford conjugation
contents.reason: The phase-aware coordinate updates and preservation of tableau pairings are proved locally.

contents.name: §20.2 Clifford circuits preserve stabilizer states
contents.reason: The tableau definition and gate-update proof absorb the conjugated-generator argument.

contents.name: §20.2–20.3 Measurement-controlled Clifford circuits and feed-forward history
contents.reason: The local definition specializes the source interface to finite deterministic histories with Pauli instrument branches and explicit zero-probability semantics.

contents.name: §20.2 Pauli observable measurement projectors M±
contents.reason: The two projectors, branch probabilities, conditional maps, and zero-branch convention are defined locally.

contents.name: Theorem 6: Gottesman–Knill exact simulation
contents.reason: The local theorem supplies exact transcript and final-ray agreement plus explicit bit and workspace bounds.

contents.name: §20.3 Deterministic commuting-measurement case
contents.reason: Maximal isotropicity, label injectivity, signed phase recovery, and zero opposite branch are proved locally.

contents.name: §20.3 Anticommuting random-measurement case
contents.reason: Fair branch weights and the old-pivot row replacement are proved with exact phase tracking.

contents.name: §20.3 Generator-only simulator and deterministic sign recovery
contents.reason: The procedure specifies measurement branching and exact signed row reduction; correctness is proved separately.

contents.name: §20.3 Optional randomized classical controller
contents.reason: The assigned circuit interface is a deterministic finite history tree; this batch makes no claim about extra controller coin tapes.

contents.name: §20.1 EPR-pair and tensor-product stabilizer examples
contents.reason: The assigned worked example is the one-qubit X measurement; entangled-state examples are not needed for this simulator result.

contents.name: §14.1 Pauli operations as two-outcome Hermitian observables
contents.reason: The local definition fixes outcomes ±1, bit labels 0 and 1, projectors, and instrument branches.

contents.name: §14.1 Spectral projectors and branch probabilities
contents.reason: Complementarity, orthogonality, nonnegative weights, and total probability are proved directly.

contents.name: §14.1 Two-outcome Pauli instrument branches used at adaptive tree nodes
contents.reason: The tree definition uses these projectors and branch weights at each observed measurement node.

contents.name: §14.1 Equal rank of the two eigenspaces of a nonidentity Pauli
contents.reason: Equal eigenspace dimensions are not used by stabilizer-circuit simulation; fairness here follows from anticommuting stabilizers.

contents.name: §14.3 Stabilizer-code definition, generators, and −I exclusion
contents.reason: The subgroup hypotheses and label-space rank are stated explicitly and their structural claims are proved locally.

contents.name: §14.3 Common +1 fixed space and its average projector
contents.reason: The finite group average is proved self-adjoint, idempotent, and exactly the common fixed-space projection.

contents.name: §14.3 Code-space dimension 2^(n−r)
contents.reason: The trace of the local average projector gives the exact dimension formula, including r=0 and r=n.

contents.name: §14.3 Repetition, Shor, Steane, five-qubit, Bell, and GHZ code examples
contents.reason: These error-correcting-code constructions belong to later QC pages; the assigned companion works one-qubit stabilizer measurement.

contents.name: §14.3 Converse: −I in the stabilizer forces a zero fixed space
contents.reason: The assigned definition excludes −I and the rank theorem proves nonzero fixed space in that case; the converse is not used by this circuit result.

contents.name: §14.1 Nondestructive Pauli measurement by phase estimation
contents.reason: The simulator consumes the abstract projective instrument directly and does not synthesize a physical measurement circuit.

contents.name: §II Phase-aware Pauli rows and binary labels
contents.reason: The tableau stores exact mod-4 phases and binary labels under the declared X^x Z^z convention.

contents.name: §II Stabilizer and destabilizer row pairing
contents.reason: The basis-state construction verifies all extended symplectic pairings, including empty row families.

contents.name: §III Clifford gate tableau updates
contents.reason: H, S, S†, and CNOT formulas preserve phase-aware rows and pairings.

contents.name: §III Random measurement pivot update
contents.reason: The local proof establishes generator independence, branch stabilization, and correct phase on each outcome.

contents.name: §III Deterministic measurement sign and row reduction
contents.reason: Binary Gaussian elimination finds the unique stabilizer product and its exact signed outcome.

contents.name: Proposition 3: tableau invariants
contents.reason: The generator and extended-tableau invariants are stated in the local tableau definition and preserved by updates.

contents.name: §III Storage and deterministic-measurement cost
contents.reason: The theorem gives dense-row workspace and O(n^3) deterministic measurement bounds.

contents.name: §IV Implementation and experimental performance
contents.reason: The assigned scope is an exact mathematical simulator and bit bound; implementation code and empirical timings are nonlogical and not included.
